source.recordedAt: date not stated in the source repo; see the source repo's own commit history for a bound
source.protocol: non-blind — for each target, the evaluator was shown exactly 3 candidate swatches, each already labeled with which algorithm proposed it (helmlab@0.14.0 top-1 / CIEDE2000 via culori@4.0.2 top-1 / OKLab ΔE via culori@4.0.2 top-1). The evaluator picked by eye from swatches alone, before looking at the metric numbers, but the algorithm-of-origin label WAS visible during selection. This is fundamentally different from the 2026 retest protocol in this repo, which hides algorithm identity, current dyeId, and all scores/ranks throughout.
source.candidateSetMethod: NOT a broad pool. The source repo filtered colorant-picker's 51 (at the time) traditional-color targets down to a warm/brown hue sector (target OKLCH h in [20deg,110deg], C >= 0.03) AND further down to cases where helmlab's top-1 nearest dye disagreed with CIEDE2000's top-1 nearest dye. Only those disagreement cases were shown to the evaluator, and only the 3 algorithms' top-1 picks were offered as candidates (not the full ~109-dye pool). This means the 4 cases here are not representative of all targets, and the candidate set for each is exactly 3 items.
source.provenanceConfidence: high for the pick itself (explicit, deliberate, recorded human judgment by a named person) — low for candidate-set breadth (only 3 algorithm-proposed candidates, not a full-pool comparison, and the 4 targets themselves were pre-selected for being disagreement cases, not a random or complete sample)
source.doNotTreatAsHumanGroundTruthDataset: These 4 cases are kept separate from the 2026 retest (data/retest/) and must not be merged into human-picks.json. They may be compared against the retest results and against the algorithmic-baseline post-hoc, per methodology.
